newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE RUBBER TRADE SAYS THAI PLAN IMPRACTICAL.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE RUBBER TRADE SAYS THAI PLAN IMPRACTICAL.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market reacted coolly to news that Thailand wants rubber producers to curb output to shore up soft prices, saying the plan was doomed to fail because it is unworkable, dealers said on Thursday.

"Not a chance in hell," one dealer said when asked if the proposal can be implemented in Southeast Asia. "It's like saying to someone if you can cut his salary. You cannot control small tappers in Thailand and Indonesia from earning a living."
Another trader said the plan may work in Malaysia, but "you need Indonesia and Thailand to make it work because they're the two biggest producers" in the world.
Trading in the market was thin. Bridgestone and Michelin were said to have bought some RSS3 rubber while local dealers engaged in modest shortcovering for RSS1 rubber.
"I think Michelin bought a small amount as part of their regular buying programme," a dealer said.
"Bridgestone was in, but most of the other players were simply not around," another dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, September RSS3 was seen at 94.25 U.S. cents a kg from 94.00 cents. September RSS1 was seen at 137.75 Singapore cents (93 U.S. cents) a kg from 137.25 cents.
